newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA DOLLAR ENDS FLAT AFTER LACKLUSTER AFTERNOON - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: CANADA DOLLAR ENDS FLAT AFTER LACKLUSTER AFTERNOON - AUG 12.

text.p: The Canadian dollar ended relatively flat on Tuesday, surrendering modest midday gains on the Bank of Canada's prediction for a stronger currency.

The Canada unit finished around C$1.3935 (US$0.7175) on Tuesday from Monday's close at C$1.3930 (US$0.7178). The currency had strengthened to C$1.3927 (US$0.7180) at midday after the release of the central bank's summer review.
"There were good two-way flows today, but we had a fairly lackluster afternoon," said one trader at a Canadian bank.
While the currency market is pressing for an interest rate hike, the Bank of Canada appears content to hold its course.
Economists told Reuters on Tuesday that currency market traders recently pushed the currency near two-year lows in a bid to test the central bank's interest rate policy.
ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett economist Andrew Pyle said that "the market feels that if it pushes the Canadian dollar to US$0.7142, it will get another rate hike."
But in its report today, the Bank of Canada predicted the currency could strengthen without a rate increase.
"Canada's strongly underlying economic fundamentals continue to support the currency market expectations that the Canadian dollar will appreciate over time," the bank said.
The Bank of Canada last raised interest rates by 25 basis points on June 26 to support the struggling Canadian dollar.
Technical Data analyst David Ebata said the bank may have to boost rates again if the unit traded down past US$0.7150.

"Canada has the second lowest interest rate environment next to Japan, and the fact that the Bank of Canada has indicated that the rate will not be going up is not good for the dollar," Ebata wrote in a report on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar rose to 83.46 Japanese yen from 83.34 on Monday and climbed to 1.3376 marks from Monday's 1.3371 marks.
